observation_summary: The compiler crashes with an UnsupportedOperationException when processing object literals containing numeric keys or getters/setters, because the Normalize pass attempts to call getString() on nodes that are not STRING or NAME types.
hypothesis: The Normalize pass incorrectly attempts to annotate constants by convention for nodes that are not NAME or STRING types (e.g., NUMBER nodes used as object literal keys), leading to an UnsupportedOperationException when calling getString() on these nodes. The logic in NormalizeStatements.visit() and annotateConstantsByConvention() fails to filter out non-string/non-name nodes before processing them.
prediction: The fix will involve adding a check in NormalizeStatements.visit() or annotateConstantsByConvention() to ensure that only nodes of type Token.NAME or Token.STRING are processed, preventing the compiler from attempting to treat numeric or other literal keys as strings.
experiment_rationale: The stack trace points directly to Node.getString() being called on a node that is not a string node, triggered by the Normalize pass. The code snippet confirms that annotateConstantsByConvention is called on nodes without verifying their type beyond the initial check in visit().
reasoning_summary: The bug is a missing validation check (Checking) in the normalization logic. The compiler assumes all nodes passed to the constant annotation logic are valid string/name nodes, but object literals can contain numeric keys or other structures that violate this assumption.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not the algorithm itself, but the lack of a guard/check for the input data type.
